question: Which of the following Mauryan inscriptions is NOT located in present-day India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandahar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kandahar** is the Mauryan inscription that is NOT located in present-day India.
 
• Kandahar is currently in modern-day Afghanistan.
 
• The other inscriptions mentioned (Kalsi, Maski, and Girnar) are all located within the geographical boundaries of present-day India.
 
• The Mauryan Empire, under rulers such as Ashoka, had inscriptions spread across a vast region, including parts of present-day India, Nepal, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Mauryan Empire** was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE and became one of the largest empires in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Ashoka, one of the most famous Mauryan emperors, is known for his widespread inscriptions and promotion of Buddhism.
 
• The inscriptions of Ashoka, written in various scripts and languages, are key historical sources for understanding the Mauryan period.
 
• These inscriptions were often engraved on rocks and pillars and served to propagate the policies and edicts of Ashoka, including his advocacy for dharma (moral law) and non-violence.
